# API Contract Requirements Checklist: Confirmation Email and Reservation Cancellation

**Purpose**: Validate the quality (completeness, clarity, consistency, measurability) of the HTTP API and error-semantics requirements in `spec.md`, `plan.md` and `contracts/api.md`, plus the email contract and the cancellation edge cases they depend on.
**Created**: 2026-11-07
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [contracts/api.md](../contracts/api.md) · [plan.md](../plan.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command from the feature context (focus: API + error semantics; depth: standard pre-implementation review; scope: spec + plan/contracts). Every item was then reviewed against `spec.md`, `contracts/api.md` and the plan at the user's request (no code involved). `✔ covered` = already met; `✎ fixed` = spec or contract edited to meet it. The user should confirm the review.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Operation Inventory & Access

- [x] CHK001 Are both new operations listed in the spec itself with method, path and sign-in requirement, or does the spec leave the paths only to the plan/contract? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006, §FR-013, Contract] ✎ fixed: FR-006 and FR-013 now name both paths and methods.
- [x] CHK002 Is "clearly marked as public" / "requiring sign-in" defined measurably (e.g. security entry, description prefix) rather than by appearance? [Clarity, Spec §FR-023, §US5] ✎ fixed: FR-023 defines public (no security entry, description prefix) vs staff (bearer security).
- [x] CHK003 Are the operation counts in the plan (19 total, 7 public) traceable to a requirement or contract section that will be updated if the count changes? [Traceability, Plan §Scale/Scope] ✎ fixed: contract §Documentation requirements states 19 operations / 7 public.
- [x] CHK004 Is the changed behavior of the existing `POST /reservations` (confirmation email, description no longer saying "No email is sent") captured as a requirement and not only as a contract note? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001, Contract §Other documented changes] ✎ fixed: FR-023 requires the POST /reservations description to mention the email; contract §Other documented changes.

## Request Rules

- [x] CHK005 Is the guest request body specified in the spec (field name `code`, type, required) or only in the contract? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006, Contract §POST /reservations/cancel] ✎ fixed: FR-006 names the required text field `code`.
- [x] CHK006 Is the required response when the code is sent in the URL (path or query) defined, given that FR-006 only says it "is not a supported form"? [Gap, Spec §FR-006] ✎ fixed: FR-006 defines the answer (standard unknown-route not found, no lookup by code).
- [x] CHK007 Are the format limits of `code` defined consistently: the spec says "wrong-length" codes get NOT_FOUND while the contract says any string is accepted with no trimming and no length limit? [Consistency, Spec §FR-011, Contract §POST /reservations/cancel] ✎ fixed: FR-011 states any text is accepted; wrong length is simply a not-found code. Spec and contract now agree.
- [x] CHK008 Is it clear which malformed-code cases produce 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR` (missing, non-string) and which produce 404 (empty string, wrong length), and is the boundary stated in the spec? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-011, §FR-022] ✎ fixed: FR-011 and contract: missing/non-string `code` and unknown fields → 400; any text value, including empty → 404.
- [x] CHK009 Does the staff operation's rule "a body is ignored" conflict with the inherited rule "unknown body fields refused"? [Conflict, Spec §FR-022, Contract §POST /reservations/{id}/cancel] ✎ fixed: FR-013/FR-022 state that bodiless operations ignore a body (as in 001 contract); strictness applies to operations with a body.
- [x] CHK010 Is a malformed reservation id on the staff operation specified consistently: 404 `NOT_FOUND` in the contract versus "all input validated before any change" with 400 in the inherited rules? [Conflict, Spec §FR-013, §FR-022, Contract] ✎ fixed: FR-013 states malformed id → not found, the documented 001 exception; contract aligned.
- [x] CHK011 Are content-type, body-size and JSON-syntax errors for the guest operation covered by explicit requirement or by a stated inheritance? [Coverage, Contract §POST /reservations/cancel] ✔ covered (contract 400 row lists bad JSON, content type, size; 001 rules inherited).

## Response & Error Semantics

- [x] CHK012 Is the order of checks (route, auth, validation, not found, conflicts) written as a requirement in the spec, or only in the plan and contract? [Traceability, Plan §Constraints, Contract intro] ✎ fixed: FR-022 now states the check order.
- [x] CHK013 Are the HTTP statuses for "not found", "cannot be cancelled" and "already cancelled" stated in the spec, or does FR-022 only say "correct HTTP status"? [Clarity, Spec §FR-022, Contract §Error codes] ✎ fixed: FR-022 lists the status per outcome (400/401/404/409/409/500).
- [x] CHK014 Is the outcome defined for a reservation that is both already cancelled and past its start (ALREADY_CANCELLED vs CANNOT_CANCEL precedence)? [Gap, Spec §FR-009, §FR-010] ✎ fixed: FR-010 and contract: ALREADY_CANCELLED takes precedence.
- [x] CHK015 Is "a clear, harmless answer" for an already cancelled reservation reconciled with returning an error status (409) while claiming the operation is "safe to repeat"? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-010, Contract §Error codes] ✎ fixed: FR-010 clarifies it is a 409 refusal with its own code, not a failure, and is safe to repeat.
- [x] CHK016 Is the single generic NOT_FOUND message specified exactly (text, shape, status) so that "identical" in FR-011 is objectively testable? [Measurability, Spec §FR-011, §SC-004] ✎ fixed: FR-011 fixes the message "Reservation not found"; contract applies it to both operations.
- [x] CHK017 Can "reveals nothing about whether a reservation exists" be verified for timing and response size as well as content, or is it limited to body and status? [Measurability, Spec §FR-011] ✎ fixed: FR-011 covers content and the timing independence from code similarity (research R6).
- [x] CHK018 Is the 200 response shape defined once and consistently between the spec (FR-012) and the contract example, including which guest fields are deliberately omitted? [Consistency, Spec §FR-012, Contract §200 response] ✎ fixed: FR-012 now also excludes guest contact data and states the ISO-8601 UTC format, matching the contract example.
- [x] CHK019 Is the `Cache-Control: no-store` requirement on the success response traceable to a spec requirement, or is it contract-only? [Traceability, Contract §POST /reservations/cancel] ✎ fixed: FR-012 requires `Cache-Control: no-store`.
- [x] CHK020 Does the status shown in affected-reservation lists (new `status: "confirmed"`) appear as a requirement with its exact response location? [Completeness, Spec §FR-019, Plan §Summary] ✎ fixed: contract states every affectedReservations item gains `status: "confirmed"`.

## Failure & Recovery Semantics

- [x] CHK021 Is the response specified when the status flip succeeds but the table or guest-slot release fails (500 in the contract) in a way consistent with "MUST NOT report success" and with the reservation staying cancelled? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008, Contract §500, Plan §Summary] ✎ fixed: FR-008 defines the 500 answer, no email, reservation stays cancelled.
- [x] CHK022 Is the result of retrying a cancellation after a partial release failure defined (ALREADY_CANCELLED vs repaired success), and is it stated whether a cancellation email is then sent exactly once? [Gap, Spec §FR-010, §FR-015, Plan §Constraints] ✎ fixed: FR-008 and contract: retry repairs the release and answers ALREADY_CANCELLED with no email.
- [x] CHK023 Is the clock used to decide "start reached" and its time-zone/DST handling specified, including the boundary at exactly the start instant? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009, §Edge Cases] ✎ fixed: FR-009 defines instant comparison against the server clock, strict at the start instant.
- [x] CHK024 Is the behavior defined for a staff cancellation of an upcoming reservation whose table was removed or whose date is now a closed date? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases, §FR-016] ✎ fixed: new edge cases (closed date still cancellable; removed table cannot affect an upcoming reservation).

## Email Contract

- [x] CHK025 Is "a way to cancel without signing in" in the spec reconciled with the contract's specific form (link with fragment plus plain code), and is the link's destination requirement defined while no customer interface exists? [Consistency, Spec §FR-001, §Assumptions, Contract §Email contract] ✎ fixed: Assumptions now describe the link-in-fragment plus plain code form and point to the contract.
- [x] CHK026 Is "avoids the full guest email address" in failure records quantified (what may appear: domain, masked local part, nothing)? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-004, §Assumptions] ✎ fixed: FR-004 and contract: no part of the address, no name, no sender message.
- [x] CHK027 Are the failure-record fields (kind, reservation, reason, time) and the log destination specified precisely enough to be asserted in an automated check? [Measurability, Spec §FR-004, §SC-002] ✎ fixed: contract §Failure record defines the log line; `at` timestamp added (also in data-model).
- [x] CHK028 Is "not delayed" quantified for a slow sender (a maximum added latency or a timeout bound), or only described as "does not wait"? [Measurability, Spec §FR-003, §SC-010, Plan §Summary] ✎ fixed: FR-003 adds the abandonment time limit (default 10 s); response bound is SC-010 (p95 < 1 s).
- [x] CHK029 Is the content of the cancellation email beyond the "You cancelled / The restaurant cancelled" wording specified (details repeated, no table name, no code)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-014, Contract §Email contract] ✎ fixed: FR-014 and contract list the details repeated and what is excluded.

## Non-Functional & Dependencies

- [x] CHK030 Is the "normal load" in SC-010 defined here or by an explicit reference to the exact feature 002 profile? [Dependency, Spec §SC-010] ✎ fixed: SC-010 now spells out the 002 SC-006 load profile.
- [x] CHK031 Is the assumption that the secret code is unguessable (entropy, no rate limiting in scope) stated or referenced, given the public, unauthenticated cancel operation? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions, §FR-006] ✎ fixed: Assumptions record the 256-bit code and rate limiting as known debt.
- [x] CHK032 Are the new configuration keys (SMTP_URL, EMAIL_FROM, timeout, restaurant name, cancel link base) and their absent/invalid behavior required by the spec, or only decided in the plan? [Traceability, Spec §Assumptions, Plan §Source Code] ✎ fixed: Assumptions state email is optional config, behavior when absent or failing, keys listed in the plan.
